title: Two-Gauss-sum hybrid split: QR is the J=1 effective-phase collapse; a const/polylog head captures the bulk of the completion cancellation
wall: W-BGK (square-root cancellation among the m=(q-1)/n Gauss-sum phases / generalized-Paley eigenvalue spectrum)
evidence: Probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/_407_consthead_split.py (exact full-order char chi via primitive_root + discrete-log table; tau_j = gaussSum(chi^{dj}, psi_b) in high-precision complex; proper dyadic mu_n at large primes q=1 mod n, beta_eff 2.8-3.7: n=8 q=953,2273; n=16 q=4129,12433; n=32 q=16417). The completion identity ||sum_{j<t} tau(chi^{dj},psi_b)|| = t*B is verified EXACTLY at every prime (err 1e-12 to 1e-9), confirming the in-tree algebra (completion_identity + I4). The NOVEL C084 hope -- that a CONSTANT/POLYLOG head J captures the bulk (S_J/full -> 1 fast, with QR = J=1 collapse) -- is REFUTED on three independent measurements: (1) the head fraction S_J/full is TINY for const/polylog J and rises ~linearly toward 1 only as J->t: at n=16 q=12433 (t=m=777), J=1 gives 0.0001, J=2 gives 0.012, J=log2(m)=10 gives 0.037, J=sqrt(m)=28 gives 0.084, reaching ~0.51 only at J=t/2 and 1.0 only at J=t (same pattern at all 5 primes); (2) the partial head S_J behaves as an INCOHERENT RANDOM WALK of flat modulus-sqrt(q) phases: a least-squares log-log fit of S_J vs J over J in [2, t/4] gives slope 0.455 ~ 0.5 (random walk = sqrt(J)), NOT 1.0 (coherent), with mean S_J/sqrt(J*q) ~ 1.12 (so S_J ~ sqrt(J*q) GROWS with J, it does not collapse); (3) the J=1 'QR collapse' term has |tau_0|=1 (the trivial-character -1), capturing fraction ~1e-4 of full -- it is the bookkeeping +1 bookmark, not a structural collapse. The genuine collapse to the small target t*B = t*sqrt(n log m) (B/sqrt(n log2 m) = 0.91-1.08 across all rows, i.e. B sits on the off-wall true law) lives ENTIRELY in the discarded triangle-inequality step ||sum_j tau_j|| <= sum_j ||tau_j|| across ALL m phases. The chi^{dj}(b) phases over an arithmetic progression of indices are NOT pinned; they equidistribute.
honest_note: PROVEN piece: both load-bearing identities the connection cites are real, axiom-clean, in-tree -- completion_identity (t*eta_b = sum_{j<t} tau(chi^{dj},psi_b), SubgroupGaussSumWorstCase.lean) and I4 tangentSum_mul_orderOf_eq_sum_jacobiSum (TangentSumJacobiAverage.lean) -- and the probe re-verifies the completion identity to fp precision. REFUTED: the connection's novel reframing, that the cancellation is graded by how many low/AP-indexed phases you can 'pin' and that a const/polylog head already captures the bulk. It does not: the head is a random walk (slope 0.5), captures O(J/t) of the structure, and the entire sqrt-cancellation lives in the all-m-phases triangle step -- the unchanged open BGK problem. This is consistent with and sharpens the earlier C039 PARTIAL (which showed the +1/t trivial-char saving is negligible); C084 additionally kills the head/tail-grading hope by measuring the random-walk exponent of the partial head directly. The QR/index-2 lane is clean only because there the COMPLEMENTARY subgroup is small (full-group Paley = the #400 trap), not the thin-mu_n prize regime. No Lean attempted (the algebra is already in-tree and verified; the substantive content is the refutation of the head-captures-bulk claim, which the probe settles). No closure. Should be logged to DISPROOF_LOG (head/tail completion split offers no BGK progress).
